posts.title: Letshuoer Cadenza 12 - A Mirror Keeps No Secrets
posts.body:
**Letshuoer Cadenza 12 2024**

12-Driver Hybrid - 6-Way Crossover
1× 10mm LSS Kevlar Dome DD
7× Sonion BA + 4× Knowles BA
5-Bore Acoustic Network

1,699 USD

Some objects tell you quite a lot before you've listened to a single track. The titanium shell does that here. Mirror polished, a fingerprint magnet, the kind of finish that demands to be handled carefully and then immediately shows you every time you didn't. That's not really a flaw. It's just what happens when the design is this legible.

**BUILD & FIT**

Titanium, small, almost custom in how it sits closer to a CIEM than most universals bother getting. The fit disappears fast, the shell small enough that it never announces itself the way bigger flagship housings tend to. The trade off is the finish. It's gorgeous under light, but prone to micro-scratches under basically anything else. It photographs perfectly and lives a little less perfectly.

**LOWS **

The bass is probably the perfect amount for me, which sounds like a non answer until you think about how rare that actually is. Nothing booms where it isn't supposed to. The 10mm dynamic driver does its job and stops, no overreach into the midrange, no bleed dressed up as "warmth" I think of this as bass with a boundary rather than bass as spectacle. It knows where to stop. 

Gen Hoshino - Sapiens 
The low end here doesn't just stay disciplined, it does something closer to devotional. The drums, the sub rumble underneath them, the whole low frequency architecture of the track, it doesn't just hit, it lifts. There's a difference between bass that impresses you and bass that moves something in you, and this felt like the second one. "Soul elevating" isn't a phrase I throw around for gear, but that's what happened here.

**MIDS**

Vocals are forward here, and forward in a way that has real texture to it, a bit throaty, in the way a voice sounds when you can hear the actual mechanism producing it rather than a smoothed over version of the same performance. Crisp, clear, and unwilling to hide anything about how a vocalist actually sounds.

Kaibutsu - YOASOBI
Ikura's vocal layering is dense here, with different textures stacked on top of each other, and less resolving gear can turn that into one blurred voice. The Cadenza keeps the throatiness intact without letting one layer wash into the other.

I'm a Controversy - Ado
Ado's vocal delivery, to me, depends on whether the gear can handle the rasp without softening it into something more palatable. The Cadenza doesn't soften it. The grain stays exactly where she put it, forward enough that you're not allowed to ignore it.

Never Let Go -  Hikaru Utada
A gentler test after that.. Utada's voice here is more restrained, less aggressive, and the same forwardness that made Ado's rasp land hard just makes this one feel intimate instead. Same tuning, completely different result. That's the part I find interesting.

**HIGHS**

The treble bites, but it's about the amount I like. Energetic without becoming something that punishes you for turning the volume up. That's a specific needle to thread = enough air and micro detail retrieval to make you rediscover a track's small edges, without crossing into sibilance. The Cadenza 12 threads it.

It's not relaxed treble, but I wouldn't call it aggressive either. It has exactly the amount of bite I want and then stops.

Path - Apocalyptica
The strings on this one can get pretty sharp if the treble isn't handled well. There's a roughness to the bowing that I actually like, and the Cadenza lets me hear it without turning that roughness into glare. The texture stays there. So does the bite.

The imaging isn't flat either. It feels spherical, with depth in every direction rather than just width, which is doing a lot of the work in making the whole presentation feel less like a stage and more like a room you are standing inside.

**CONCLUDING NOTES**

The Cadenza doesn't really dominate any one category for me. I think its strength is that I never find myself wanting something that's badly missing from it. I think that's where most of its appeal comes from. Bass that knows its boundary, mids that don't flatter a vocalist into something safer, treble with exactly the bite it needs and not a decibel more. This is the ultimate vocal jpop set for me.

Thanks to a dear friend for the recommendation. My wallet would like to formally register a complaint, but unfortunately he is not responsible for my inability to exercise restraint.

**SOURCE**

FiiO KA17 on high gain.

**EARTIPS USED**

Divinus Velvet Narrow Bore and Spinfit W1.

**TRACKS**

Shogeki - Yuko Ando 
Zankyosanka - Aimer
Ref:rain - Aimer 
I'm a Controversy - Ado

posts.title: ZiiGaat Horizon - A Little Spice Goes a Long Way
posts.body:
**ZiiGaat Horizon**

5 Drivers, Tribrid
1x 10mm Bio-cellulose DD
2x Knowles BA
2x Custom Composite Planar

329 USD 

The Horizon is ZiiGaat's tribrid, and my first impression was a fun, energetic signature with a little airiness up top that I liked right away.

**BUILD & FIT -**

3D-printed resin shell with 0.78mm 2-pin connector. The fit didn't hold up for me over a long session. After about two hours of use I started experiencing discomfort and ear pain because of the size and shape of the shell, so comfort will depend a lot on your ears.

**LOWS -**

The bass is tastefully done, and adequate. It doesn't try to overdo anything, but it can hit when a track asks for it.

Never Let Go - Hikaru Utada
I tried this at the highest volume I could tolerate, and the bass notes slapped me in the face, in a good way.

Despite its controlled presentation, the Horizon can deliver some serious impact.

**MIDS -**

Vocals are nice and intimate, though a bit thin. They sit close to you, which suits a set with this much going on up top.

Zankyosanka - Aimer
The Demon Slayer Entertainment District opening, fast and dramatic. Aimer's voice sits close and intimate, and the airy treble gives the band moving around her some extra sparkle and presence.

**HIGHS -**

The spicy treble is one of my favourite aspects of the Horizon.

I quite like the little bit of airiness up top. It isn't harsh, and it adds some extra pop. The airiness comes from the planar drivers, which I found interesting. The treble can be a bit grainy, and it could be a bit bright for treble-sensitive people.

**TECHNICALITIES -**

Great detail and separation. Imaging is great too, especially on stringed instruments.

Path - Apocalyptica
Apocalyptica is built around cellos, so this track is mostly bowed strings. That makes it a good test for the imaging on stringed instruments, and the Horizon places each one clearly.

This was one of the more enjoyable demonstrations of its imaging capabilities.

**CONCLUDING NOTES -**

I like this. Fun and energetic. Detail retrieval, separation, and imaging are particular highlights, making it an engaging listen without feeling overly analytical. The shell and the spicy treble are the catches. 

**SOURCES USED -**

CrinEar Protocol Max & Apple Dongle.

**EARTIPS USED - **

Stock silicone tips.

posts.title: Endgame Gear OP1 8K V2 Review
posts.body:
**White & Dark Frost**

I have used quite a few mice over the years, but the OP1 8K V2 is probably the first one in a while that has made me lose interest in looking for something else. I initially got the White version, but it had an issue, and GenesisPC helped me get it replaced with the Dark Frost. I have stuck with the Dark Frost ever since, which should tell you enough about how much I like this mouse.

\n\n![152983.jpg](assets/posts/1793919283267-inline-152983.jpg)\n\n

Starting with the shape, because that is easily my favourite part.

I have 19×9 cm hands and use a claw-fingertip hybrid grip. The OP1 might look rather small and narrow, but it works exceptionally well for me. I particularly like the sides, as they let me position my fingers freely without the shape dictating where they should go. At the same time, the narrow and rather aggressive profile gives me a very secure, locked in feeling. I get the freedom to adjust my grip while still having enough contact with the mouse to maintain stability.

I also like that I am not entirely dependent on either my palm or fingertips. It is a bit of both. I can use the rear contact for stability while still making adjustments with my fingers. The shorter length and narrow front work particularly well with this, giving me plenty of room for micro adjustments without feeling like I am fighting the shape.

Tracking, flicking, micro adjustments, you name it. I find the OP1 comfortable and easy to control across the board. More importantly, I dont have to keep thinking about where my fingers should be or constantly readjusting my grip. I just pick it up and use it.

I know the shape wont be for everyone, and I would not recommend it based on hand size alone. But for my grip, this is about as good as it gets. It is also the most comfortable mouse I have used, which is probably the biggest reason I keep going back to it.

\n\n![149110.jpg](assets/posts/1793919349666-inline-149110.jpg)\n\n

Moving on to the hardware, EGG has done a pretty damn good job here.

The Kailh GX switches feel fantastic. They are crisp, responsive and have a satisfying actuation. They are light without feeling flimsy, and I particularly like how effortless they are to spam. The click latency implementation is equally impressive. The OP1 has topped the latency and click testing I have seen, and EGG deserves credit for getting this right.

8K polling is one thing, implementing it properly is another. The PAW3950 sensor and polling implementation have been flawless in my experience. I would not go as far as claiming that 8K polling is going to magically transform your aim, but it is nice knowing that you are getting a properly executed implementation rather than another specification thrown onto a product for marketing purposes.

The coating is another highlight. It is genuinely one of the best I have used. Good grip, nice feel and nothing that makes me want to immediately reach for grip tape(Which i genuinely hate). Combined with the shape, it makes the mouse feel very secure in hand.

The stock skates are good too. Nothing particularly exciting to write home about, but that is not necessarily a bad thing. They work well enough, but i ended up replacing them with Magic Ice full skates and Dream Gamer Saturn dot skates.

The cable is pretty good for a wired mouse. Obviously, wireless is convenient, and I am not going to pretend a cable does not exist, but with a proper setup, it is not something I find particularly bothersome. I eventually switched to a ForkyMods cable though, which is a nice little upgrade.

The scroll wheel is good as well. Nice scrolling feel, defined steps and no real complaints. Although, I would not put too much faith in the whole dustproof encoder terminology. All scroll wheels can eventually develop dust related issues. Calling something dustproof is not going to save it from the inevitable.

I have seen quite a bit of criticism directed towards the scroll wheel especially on places like reddit, but personally, I think it is perfectly good enough. It does what I need it to do, and I dont have any particular complaints about it.

Software is simple and does what it needs to. I dont particularly enjoy having to install unnecessarily complicated software just to configure a mouse, so EGG keeping things straightforward is appreciated.

**Conclusion -**

So what I am basically getting at is that the overall package is very good, especially considering the price.

Flawless 8K polling, excellent click latency, great switches, great coating, decent stock skates, a decent cable, a decent scroll wheel, simple software and solid support. There is very little here that feels like a compromise.

But if there is one thing that makes the OP1 special to me, it is the shape(I know i might be parroting alot about the shape, but years of trying different shapes and finally finding your holy grail has that effect). All the specifications in the world would not mean much if I did not enjoy actually using the thing this much. As the community says = **Shape is King.**

Of course, shape is subjective, and I would not recommend it blindly to everyone. But if it works for your grip, I genuinely think it is one of the best options out there.

For me, it is easily the most comfortable mouse I have used. And at this point, I dont really see a reason to look elsewhere.

posts.title: Endgame Gear Op1 8K V2 Modding Guide
posts.body:
There are quite a few ways to customise the OP1, should you feel the need to.

**Cable -**
If you are looking to replace the stock cable, you have a few options. ForkyMods and PMM Flexcord are worth considering.

ForkyMods cables are custom orders, so you will have to get in touch with the owner directly through Discord (username - 4qg) or you can find him on the official Endgame Gear discord server. The downside is the delivery time, which can be quite long, especially if you are outside Europe.

I would personally avoid the Midori cable. They have a reputation for being prone to breaking and I dont think they are worth the gamble.

Another option is a Hevitas cable from Taobao, GooFish/Xianyu. It is a cheaper alternative that still gets the job done, so worth looking into if you dont want to spend too much on a cable.

Alternatively, you can braid the stock cable yourself, following the method shown by Viscose in one of their videos.


![153101.jpg](assets/posts/1793924906151-inline-153101.jpg)


**Bungee -**
VAXEE Oryza
Zowie Camade II
Razer Mouse Bungee
You can try other bungees as well.

**Base -**
You can either 3D print your own base or buy one. There are both free and paid files available online, but dont just send a file to a print shop and call it a day. The printing material, orientation and settings matter if you want a decent result.(I am speaking from personal experience after a failed attempt)

ForkyMods also offers a base, particularly worth considering if you are using a glasspad. However, I would not recommend it for clothpad users.

There are cheaper alternatives on Taobao and GooFish as well. Just be careful when buying files or printed bases, since some sellers are selling stolen designs. Make sure you are buying from a legitimate seller.


![152965.jpg](assets/posts/1793924951771-inline-152965.jpg)


**Scroll Wheel -**
The ForkyMods scroll wheel is optional. Personally, I dont think it makes a particularly meaningful difference over the stock wheel and saving 1.3 grams is not exactly going to change your life.

If you do want to replace it, though, ForkyMods is probably the cheapest and best option. I would not recommend the expensive option from PMM.

**Shell Mods -**
Complete shell modding is optional too. There are quite a few routes you can take, ranging from PMM kits to custom lightweight body kits. You can also find fingertip oriented shells on GooFish/Xianyu.

I would look into these only if you have a specific reason to change the shape or reduce the weight. There is little point in spending money to modify something that already works perfectly well for you.


![152964.jpg](assets/posts/1793925013169-inline-152964.jpg)


**GX-Compatible Switches -**

**Kailh -**
GX (80M) - Stock Reference. 50-55gf. Balanced tactility, medium click force, high spammability. Verified OP1 GX Mode compatible.

White Sword/Blade - High tactility with a snappy, stiff rebound profile.

**Huano -**
Trasparent White shell, white dot - Standard mechanical 3-pin setup.

Transparent Purple shell, white dot - Soft end/cushion feel, highly spammable.

Transparent Green shell, white dot - Middle-ground tactile response.

Transparent Yellow shell, white dot - Snappy and stiff actuation.

Transparent Blue shell, red dot - Middle-ground feel; direct upgrade over pink dot.

Transparent Blue shell, pink dot - 55-60gf (BSPD 80m). Crisp tactile bump.

Black shell, blue dot - Fast rebound and poppy tactile profile.

Black shell, pink dot - Fast rebound with a crisp tactile snap.

Black shell, red dot - Fast rebound and poppy tactile profile.

Black shell, white dot - Standard mechanical tactile snap.

Blue shell, pink dot - Standard mechanical 3-pin setup.

Blue shell, white dot - Snappy/stiff actuation.

Blue shell, blue dot - Snappy/stiff actuation.

**HNCHK -**
Transparent Black shell, purple plunger (150M) - 60-70gf. High click force and high tactility. Verified OP1 GX Mode compatible.

Transparent Purple shell, purple dot - Standard 3-pin mechanical setup.

Transparent Purple shell, green dot - Assumption/Highly likely compatible.

Transparent Orange shell, orange dot - Assumption/Highly likely compatible.

**Zippy -**
P1 Orange dot (EGG Orange Dot) - Fast spring return with a poppy click profile.

P1 White dot (DF3-P1) - Fast rebound and high spammability.

P1 Blue dot (DF3-P1L0 5M) - 50-80gf. Medium click force, medium tactility, high spammability. Verified OP1 GX Mode compatible.

**Omron -**
D2F-01F - Extremely crisp, low-force feel (~50-60g). Requires swapping to a D2FC top housing/plunger to correct the taller Japanese housing height and prevent shell binding.

D2F-F-3-7 - Distinct click feel; keep standard Japanese housing height considerations in mind.

**Cherry -**
DG2 - Standard mechanical 3-pin setup.

**TTC -**
Gold 30M - Standard mechanical 3-pin setup.

Gold 60M - Standard mechanical 3-pin setup.

Gold 80M - Higher lifespan rating; stiffer leaf tension.

Gold 100M (marketed as 1HM) - Distinct, crisp metallic snap.

**C&K -**
ZMA030 - Lightest consistently available switch (~45-50gf). Its taller plastic actuator may require slight sanding to achieve proper shell clearance. This is an irreversible modification, so proceed carefully.

**Note -**
One thing worth mentioning is that the newer Pink Raw Input version comes with a hotswap PCB and EGG's own selection of switches. This makes experimenting with different switches considerably easier, without having to worry about manually desoldering and soldering them every time.

**Switch Compatibility -**
When using loose mechanical microswitches from the compatibility list, you will need a dedicated hotswap PCB for solderless, plug and play installation. This includes the official Endgame Gear Universal Switch PCBs and compatible aftermarket socketed boards.

**Warning-** Not all switches have pins of exactly the same thickness. If the pins are too thick, dont force them into the sockets. You could end up widening or damaging the contacts, which might make thinner pins sit loosely afterwards. Check the fit before pushing anything in.

The standard OP1 switch modules come with factory soldered switches, so you can't simply drop loose switches into the stock daughterboards. You will need to desolder the existing switches and solder the replacements manually if you are not using a hotswap PCB.

While the switches listed share a standard 3-pin physical layout, that does not necessarily mean every switch will be a perfect drop in fit. Depending on your particular build, minor adjustments may be required. For example, lightly sanding down the top plunger stem on the C&K ZMA030 or swapping the top housing on the Omron D2F-01F may be necessary to achieve proper shell clearance and pre travel spacing.


![152961.jpg](assets/posts/1793925163623-inline-152961.jpg)


**Final Thoughts -**
The OP1 shape is definitely an acquired taste. Not everyone is going to be willing to put up with its narrow profile and relatively small size. And once you start getting into cables, bungees and all the additional modifications, the investment can add up rather quickly.

That said, none of this is necessary. The OP1 is perfectly fine in its stock configuration. Dont feel the need to throw money at modifications just because they are available. There is a difference between improving something and modifying it for the sake of modifying it.

Personally, I consider the OP1 my benchmark for what a mouse should be. In my opinion, it is the best mouse ever produced. Obviously, that is a subjective statement, but I have not come across anything that has made me want to change my mind.

**Credits -**
Switch compatibility & testing data: 4qg/forkymods.com(contact reliability testing and switch feel notes)

Guide & modding content: End(me) - cable, base, scroll wheel, shell modifications and build related information.
